title: A Compass for the Wreck
premise: Salvage diver Theo Marchetti is hired to strip a wrecked survey vessel in a river delta the navy has sealed off, and he finds evidence the ship was scuttled to hide a fraud: a gold concession built on falsified coordinates. A dying prospector named Elias Voss trades him a hand-drawn map to the true source for a promise to deliver it to Voss's estranged daughter, and Theo realizes the map, the wreck, and the concession permits all point to the same crime. Racing upstream against expiring permits, pursued by the mining company's enforcer and shadowed by a navy investigator who may be friend or trap, Theo must choose between selling the map, honoring his promise, or exposing everything. In the end he reaches the forbidden source, delivers the map to Voss's daughter — who turns out to be the company's own land surveyor — and together they force the truth into the open, winning justice at the cost of the salvage fortune that started it all.
about_author: Freya Thornbury is a former marine cartographer who spent six years charting remote river systems before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels from a houseboat on the northern coast, where she claims the tide keeps her honest.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Theo Marchetti's POV. Diving the sealed survey wreck in the delta, Theo recovers instruments and notices deliberate scuttle marks — holes punched from inside. His crew boss warns him to log nothing unusual. The beat is unease: the job that pays well suddenly feels like complicity.

chapters.title: A Promise at Gunpoint of Time
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On shore leave he finds prospector Elias Voss dying in a flophouse, shot and feverish. Voss presses a oilskin-wrapped map into his hands and extracts a promise: take it to his daughter, Mara Voss, in the concession town. The beat is reluctant obligation born from pity.

chapters.title: What the Instruments Recorded
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, with a flashback. Examining the salvaged survey logs, Theo matches Voss's map coordinates to the wreck's falsified charts — the concession was staked on shifted data, stealing the source from its rightful claimants. The beat is dawning understanding: the map is evidence, not treasure.

chapters.title: The Man from Meridian Consolidated
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A polished company man, Aldous Crane, offers triple pay to buy 'any curiosities' from the wreck site. Theo lies smoothly and refuses, then finds his boat searched overnight. The beat is fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Dead Water
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. His dive partner Rennie disappears after asking too many questions; his skiff is found burned. Theo understands the company erases people, not just paper. He decides to run the river before his own permit window closes. The beat is grief converted to resolve.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He provisions quietly, hires taciturn pilot Sef Okafor, and slips past the navy cordon at night through a side channel. First contact with the river's dangers: snags, shallows, a patrol spotlight. The beat is exhilaration laced with dread.

chapters.title: The Investigator Who Drowns Slowly
chapters.summary: Navy investigator Lieutenant Cora Ives's POV. Ives pulls Theo from a capsized rapid, officially arresting him for salvage violations while privately suspecting the wreck was murder, not accident. She needs his evidence as much as he needs her protection. The beat is wary, transactional alliance.

chapters.title: Voss's Daughter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In the concession town Theo locates Mara Voss — and discovers she is Meridian's senior land surveyor, the very woman whose name authenticates the fraudulent charts. He withholds the map. The beat is betrayal and recalibration: the promise just got complicated.

chapters.title: Concessions Expiring
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara reviews the permit filings and finds anomalies she'd been trained not to see: her father's original claim, legally valid, buried under Meridian's resurvey. Her loyalty to the company cracks. The beat is quiet horror at one's own complicity.

chapters.title: Crane's Hospitality
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Crane invites Theo to dinner, reveals he knows about the map, and makes an offer wrapped around a threat: sell it, or Voss's death becomes a pattern. Theo stalls, learns Crane personally led the scuttling crew. The beat is cold terror under civilized manners.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: Theo and Ives's alternating POV. Theo breaks out of town with Ives's grudging help; they flee upriver together ahead of Crane's hired gunboats. A running chase through fog banks and deadfalls. The beat is trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: The Old Claim Shanty
chapters.summary: Ives's POV. Sheltering in Voss's abandoned claim shanty, Ives finds his journals — proof of the original strike and of threats made years ago. She must decide whether to arrest Theo or adopt his cause. The beat is an investigator choosing conscience over chain of command.

chapters.title: Rapids of the Split Channel
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The river splits; the map shows only one survivable channel. Sef reads the water while gunboats close behind. They shoot the rapids, losing most of their supplies but shaking pursuit. The beat is white-knuckle triumph with a cost.

chapters.title: Sef's Country
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef reveals he grew up on this river and that Meridian's dredging poisoned his family's fishing grounds — his silence was bought, his help now is repayment. The theme of justice outside the law deepens. The beat is confession and shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara catches up overland, having copied the permit files and burned her career doing it. She brings the legal key: her countersignature can invalidate the fraudulent resurvey if witnessed at the source itself. The beat is a defector offering the weapon Theo lacks.

chapters.title: Crane Closes the River
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Crane, tipped by a traitor among the outfitters, seals the headwater canyon and takes Sef hostage, demanding the map and Mara's signature. Deadline pressure doubles: permits expire in four days. The beat is despair and the narrowing of options.

chapters.title: What the Wilderness Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo and Mara's POV. Using Voss's map's second layer — old smuggler routes — they bypass the canyon via a sinkhole cave system. Inside, they find the bones of Voss's first partner, murdered decades ago. The beat is solemnity: this greed is generational.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They emerge above the canyon at dawn: the true source, a spring-fed pool feeding the whole river, exactly where Voss's map says. Crane arrives with Sef at gunpoint. Standoff on the rocks. The beat is arrival and immediate peril.

chapters.title: Witnesses at the Headwater
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. Mara signs the corrective affidavit at the source with Ives and Sef as witnesses; Crane orders shots fired, but his own hired men balk when Ives reads them the murder charges waiting downstream. In the struggle Crane falls into the sinkhole channel. The beat is explosive catharsis — law and wilderness converging.

chapters.title: Permits and Promises
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. With the affidavit filed and the navy moving on Meridian, Theo faces his choice: the salvage rights to the wreck are now worthless, seized as evidence. He honors Voss's promise fully, handing Mara the map as inheritance rather than leverage. The beat is bittersweet integrity.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara re-stakes her father's original claim legally, hiring Sef as river warden; Ives files her report naming the scuttling crew, accepting career damage. Justice arrives outside the courtroom, through signatures, testimony, and stubbornness. The beat is restoration.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. Months later, Theo dives the wreck one last time — now an official investigation site — and leaves the survey instruments on the riverbed where they belong. He passes Mara's new claim marker on his way out of the delta. The beat is peace earned: some things are worth more than salvage.
